one-dimension.stack.title: One Dimension
one-dimension.stack.enabled.tooltip: Stack the dimensions into one world, each a band of its height: dig through the floor of one and you fall into the next. Off, this is an ordinary world.
one-dimension.stack.loop.tooltip: Falling out of the bottom of the lowest dimension brings you back in at the top of the highest, through a portal you can see through. Off, the bottom is simply the bottom.
one-dimension.stack.included.tooltip: Whether this dimension is part of the one world. Left out, it stays a dimension of its own.
one-dimension.stack.included.overworld: The overworld is always part of it: it is the world itself.
one-dimension.stack.gap.tooltip: Empty blocks between %s and the next world below it. 0 puts its floor right on the next world's roof.
one-dimension.stack.trim.tooltip: Each world is only as tall as its players can use. The Nether ends at its roof, without the 128 empty blocks above it.
one-dimension.stack.skies.tooltip: Each world has its own sky: a world above casts no shadow on the one below, and a world without a sky, like the Nether, stays dark whatever is above it.
one-dimension.stack.bedrock.tooltip: Turn the bedrock floors and roofs between the worlds into another block, so they can be dug through. The End keeps its bedrock: it is part of the exit portal.
one-dimension.stack.bedrock.block.toolti: The block bedrock becomes, as its id, like minecraft:obsidian or minecraft:deepslate.
one-dimension.stack.spawn.tooltip: The world players start in, and come back to when they die without a bed or respawn anchor of their own.
one-dimension.stack.portals.tooltip: 8:1: one block in the Nether is eight in the overworld, so travelling through the Nether saves distance. 1:1: a portal takes you to the same X and Z, as if you had dug straight down.
